text:
dana: Heads up — deploy-bot just paused the canary for customer-api (chart v2.4.0). 3/5 pods FailedScheduling, 2/5 OOMKilled. Looks like a nodeAffinity change slipped into the values override and an unintended JVM heap bump. Can we decide pin vs rollback? @sam @maria

deploy-bot: Canary health check FAILED for release customer-api-prod (v2.4.0).
- Events: 3 FailedScheduling, 2 OOMKilled
- Traffic: canary paused, 0% to canary, all to stable
- Metrics: error_rate x3.2 for canary window
Dashboard: https://grafana.internal/r/abc123/canary/customer-api

sam: scanning events — the values override added: affinity.nodeAffinity.requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution.nodeSelector.gpu: true which restricts to gpu nodes. Also noticed env "JVM_MAX_HEAP" was set to 1g higher than stable. That explains OOMs when JVM warmed.

maria: omg, v2.4.0 defaults include that affinity? I thought it was opt-in. Looks like the chart bump introduced a changed default values.yaml.

dana: options: 1) rollback helm release to v2.3.7 (fast, revert everything) 2) pin release to v2.3.7 and apply hotfix chart 2.4.1 (patch affinity default + revert heap override). Which minimizes customer impact? We have dedicated capacity SLA.

ops-oncall: If rollback, note DB migration hooks are no-op for this chart, so rollback is straightforward. If we pin+hotfix, we need a quick chart lint + smoke e2e and then re-run canary. Pin+hotfix is lower blast radius if we can ship within ~30m.

sam: I can cut hotfix 2.4.1. Quick patch will set affinity default back to nil and remove the JVM override. Command to run in CI: ```helm upgrade customer-api ./charts/customer-api --namespace prod --reuse-values --version 2.4.1 --set affinity.nodeAffinity.requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution.nodeSelector.gpu=false --set env.JVM_MAX_HEAP=1536m``` Or alternatively patch via kubectl to remove the nodeSelector on the canary pods for immediate relief: ```kubectl patch deployment customer-api-canary -n prod --type=json -p='[ {"op":"remove","path":"/spec/template/spec/affinity/nodeAffinity/requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution"} ]'```

maria: I'm OK with pin+hotfix provided we get the hotfix pushed quickly and re-run canary at 50% traffic. I'll review release notes and the values diffs. Add a note in release notes that defaults reverted and heap override removed.

deploy-bot: Manual action required: a release pin has been requested by dana. Current stable pinned at v2.3.7. Canary remains paused.

dana: Pinned stable to v2.3.7 and rolled back live traffic. I've drafted release-notes internal doc at /docs/release-notes/2026-03-20-customer-api.md — please add the hotfix blurb. @sam please cut 2.4.1 and @maria please review notes. I'll watch the cluster.

sam: Starting hotfix build, running chart-lint and smoke tests now. ETA ~18m. Will post CI link when green.

maria: Review done, added: 
- "Fix: accidental nodeAffinity default causing scheduling on GPU-only nodes"
- "Fix: unintended JVM heap override removed from values.yaml"
- Instructions: how to rollback/pin locally (helm rollback + helm history) and who to page if canary re-fails.

dana: :thumbsup: Also adding a new checklist item to the canary runbook: diff values.yaml between chart versions and block default changes that add affinity or resource raises without an explicit opt-in flag.

ops-oncall: after hotfix we should run a targeted canary with 50% traffic for 10m, confirm error_rate <= 1.2x and no scheduling events. If green, then full rollout. If still failing, we'll rollback to v2.3.7 and open a postmortem.

sam: CI green, chart lint OK, smoke e2e passed. Pushing 2.4.1 now.

deploy-bot: Release 2.4.1 published by sam. Canary resume request queued — awaiting ops approval for 50% traffic shift.

maria: approving resume. starting 50% canary now.

deploy-bot: Canary resumed at 50% traffic. Monitor window started.

dana: monitoring logs & metrics. so far so good, no FailedScheduling. memory profiles look back to baseline. Good work team, will follow up with release notes update and a tiny post-deploy checklist entry.
